name: Blackberry Wine No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: sugar to every ten quarts of the liquor
ingredients.originalText: one pound of sugar to every ten quarts of the liquor

instructions.text: Put berries into a large wood or stone vessel with a tap
Pour on sufficient boiling water to cover them
When cool enough to bear your hand, bruise well until all the berries are broken
Cover up and let stand until berries begin to rise to top, which will occur in three or four days
Draw off the clear juice in another vessel
Add one pound of sugar to every ten quarts of the liquor and stir thoroughly
Let stand six to ten days in first vessel with top
Steep four ounces of isinglass in a pint of wine for twelve hours
Boil it over a slow fire till all dissolved
Place dissolved isinglass in a gallon of blackberry juice and boil them together
Let stand a few days to ferment and settle
Draw off and keep in a cool place

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put berries into a large wood or stone vessel with a tap
2. Pour on sufficient boiling water to cover them
3. When cool enough to bear your hand, bruise well until all the berries are broken
4. Cover up and let stand until berries begin to rise to top, which will occur in three or four days
5. Draw off the clear juice in another vessel
6. Add one pound of sugar to every ten quarts of the liquor and stir thoroughly
7. Let stand six to ten days in first vessel with top
8. Draw off through a jelly-bag
9. Steep four ounces of isinglass in a pint of wine for twelve hours
10. Boil it over a slow fire till all dissolved
11. Place dissolved isinglass in a gallon of blackberry juice and boil them together
12. Pour all into the vessel
13. Let stand a few days to ferment and settle
14. Draw off and keep in a cool place
